title: Valid Palindrome
statement: Given a string s, return True if it is a palindrome considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring case, otherwise return False. A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

hint: Two pointers are the classic approach, but for Python the cleanest trick is to build a filtered string and compare it with its reverse.

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

title: Two Sum
statement: Given a list of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. You may assume each input has exactly one solution and you may not use the same element twice. Return the indices in any order.
hint: Instead of a nested loop (O(n^2)), store each number's index in a dictionary. For each new number, check whether target - number is already in the dict.

title: Flatten a Nested List
statement: Given a nested list of integers (lists can be nested to any depth), return a single flattened list containing all the integers in their original order.
hint: Recursion is natural here: for each element, if it is a list, extend with flatten(element); otherwise append it.

title: Nth Fibonacci Number
statement: Write a function fib(n) that returns the nth Fibonacci number, where fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1. Try to make it efficient for larger n.
hint: Naive recursion recomputes the same values. Either keep two running values in a loop, or memoize with a dictionary / functools.lru_cache.

title: Group Anagrams
statement: Given a list of strings words, group the anagrams together. Two words are anagrams if they contain the same letters in a different order. Return the groups in any order.
hint: Use the sorted letters of each word as a dictionary key, then collect words into the matching bucket.
